To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
binuclear zirconocene complexes with μ-CH 3 bridges are present in homogeneous Ziegier-Natta catalyst systems, and that the presence of such complexes can be beneficial for the catalytic performance.

binuclear cations of the type [«Cp2MX)ilL-CHR)]+ are formed by the reaction of Cp2MX and B(C6F 5)3 in solution and are the precursors to the mononuclear active cations [«Cp 2MX)CH3(C3 H6)]+' that are formed upon the addition of propene.

binuclear zirconium cations are observed in C 6D6 solutions of zirconium dimethyl complexes and B(C6F 5)3 and that the binuclear species is a key component in the catalyst system rac-CH3)2 Si (indenyl)2 Zr (CH 3 ) 2 /Bu3NH + /B (C6F 5 ) 3.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the reactivity of zirconocene cationic complexes with Lewis acids, with the synthesis of new zirconocene complexes and the characterization of their reactivity, with the development of homogeneous Ziegler­Natta catalyst systems and with the study of their reactivity and their application in polymerization reactions.
the development of new homogeneous Ziegler- Natta catalysts.
the development of new catalysts for olefin polymerizations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binuclear cations observed in solution have no significant role in the catalytic polymerization of propylene.
the binuclear cations are not the active catalyst species but rather that the binuclear ions are a source of the more active mononuclear cations.

the binuclear zirconocene species [«C5R5)2ZrrCH3)il-CH3)]+ is present as a minor species in the catalyst systems under study, but that the binuclear cations do not act as catalysts for the polymerization reactions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the formation of binuclear species in the presence of B(C6F 5 )3 is a phenomenon that is not restricted to the (C5H 5 )2Zr(CH 3 )2/B(C6F 3 )3 system but can be observed for other zirconium dimethyl complexes as well.
binuclear species are observed in the presence of excess of the dimethy1 zirconocene complex and in the presence of an excess of B(C 6 F5)3' but are not observed in the presence both of excesses.
the presence of a binuclear cation in homogeneous Ziegher-Natta catalyst systems is not a prerequisite for a high polymerization activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binuclear species is not an active catalyst.
the binuclear zirconocene ion is a catalyst precursor and that the activity of the catalyst system is increased by the addition of the zirconocene dimethyle.
, under certain circumstances, the active catalyst species in Ziegler-Nattapolymerization systems can exist in solution in the form of binuclear cations.
